newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African firm says helping PNG fight rebels.
newsitem.headline: South African firm says helping PNG fight rebels.

text.p: South African mercenary firm Executive Outcomes said on Tuesday it would help the Papua New Guinea government in its nine year-old fight against successionist rebels.
The firm said it would provide consultancy assistance, aircraft, equipment and specialist training to Papua New Guinea armed forces.

The statement follows earlier confirmation from Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan that his government had hired mercenaries as advisers to accompany local troops on a mission against the Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA).

Executive Outcomes, Africa's best known private army which has helped Angola and Sierra Leone fight rebels, said it had been sub-contracted by British-based military consultancy Sandline International which was recently awarded a contract in the South Pacific country.

"Executive Outcomes has been sub-contracted to train the Papau New Guinea security forces as part of the many faceted strategy to reach a lasting solution to the nine year-old crisis in Bougainville," the group said.

"(It) has been sub-contracted along with other professional and reputable private companies, to provide consultancy assistance, aircraft, equipment and specialist training to the government of Papau New Guinea," the firm said.
Chan told reporters on Tuesday 40 military advisers were now training troops and would be part of a mission to the island of Bougainville targeting rebel leaders.
"They are out here to build up the capabilities of our defence force," said Chan, adding that the decision to use mercenaries was taken 18 months ago.
On Monday he had said his country had no plans to use mercenaries to fight on Bougainville, but that Sandlines would be used to help train government soldiers fighting there.
